@timestamp.short: When the document's event happened, or the record was written.
@timestamp.description: The moment the document describes, as an RFC 3339 date-time with offset. For a day record it is the day's start in the day's zone; for an event it is when the event happened; for a plan file it is when the file was written. Required on records and events; a plan file that omits it is read as "now".

labels.description: Custom key/value pairs that travel with the document and mean nothing to the app. Keys are lower case with underscores; values are strings. For anything the schema does not name: a coach's client id, a spreadsheet row, a note to self.

tags.description: A list of short keywords for filtering ("cut", "meet-prep", "travel").

mealstack.version.short: The MealStack Schema version the document follows.
mealstack.version.description: The version of the MealStack Schema the document is written against, as a semantic version string. A reader refuses a major version it does not know and reads any minor or patch version at or below the one it was built for. The `.mealstack` plan file format 1 carries `"mealstack": 1` instead and predates this field; format 2 carries `mealstack.version`.

mealstack.kind.description: What the document is, which says which field sets are present. A `plan` carries `plan.*` and its stacks, meals and ingredients; a `shelf` carries meals or ingredients on their own with no plan; a `day` is one day's record; an `event` is one telemetry event; a `proposal` is something Coach offered that the person has not accepted.

mealstack.author.description: What wrote the document: the app itself, the MealStack skill running in a model, Coach, or a person by hand. Used to say where a stack or a meal came from and to decide how much to trust a stated figure.

mealstack.author.version.short: The version of what wrote it.
mealstack.author.version.description: The version of the app, skill or Coach model that wrote the document.

macros.kcal.description: Kilocalories, always 4 × protein + 4 × carbs + 9 × fat. Derived, never independent: a writer may include it for readers that cannot multiply, and a reader recomputes it and ignores the stored value.

ingredient.id.description: A stable identifier: starts with a letter, then letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. Built-in ids are short and unprefixed (`chicken_raw`, `rice_cooked`). An ingredient declared in a file is prefixed `import.` on import so it can never collide with a built-in one; a person's own is prefixed `custom.`.

ingredient.name.short: As it appears on a plate.
ingredient.name.description: The ingredient's name as it appears on a plate and in search.

ingredient.unit.description: The unit the figures are for. Quantities of this ingredient are always in this unit: grams for a gram ingredient, cups for a cup ingredient, scoops for a scoop ingredient. A cup is 240 ml.

ingredient.per.short: The macros in exactly one unit (a `macros`).
ingredient.per.description: The macros in exactly one unit of the ingredient. Per gram for a gram ingredient, per ounce for an ounce ingredient, per piece, cup, spoon, scoop, packet or bottle otherwise. Ceilings above which a figure is refused as being for the wrong unit: 9.1 kcal per gram, 260 per ounce, 50 per tsp, 140 per tbsp, 1,000 per cup or each, 400 per scoop or packet, 800 per bottle.

ingredient.qualifier.description: What the figure is for, so two figures for one ingredient tell apart: "raw weight", "cooked weight", "from the label", "1 cup = 240 ml".

ingredient.source.description: Built into the app, the person's own, or an import.

ingredient.built_in_version.short: The release of the built-in ingredients the figure is from.
ingredient.built_in_version.description: For a built-in ingredient, which release of the built-in ingredients the figures are from, so a plate priced against an older release can be re-priced when a figure is corrected.

portion.id.description: A UUID for the line, so an edit can address one of two identical lines.

portion.quantity.short: How much, in the ingredient's unit.
portion.quantity.description: How much of the ingredient, in its own unit. Positive. Caps per unit above which a line is refused as not a plate: 2,000 g, 64 oz, 24 each, 8 cups, 16 tbsp, 24 tsp, 6 scoops, 6 packets, 6 bottles. A line over 1,500 kcal is refused whatever the unit.

portion.macros.short: What the line comes to, derived (a `macros`).
portion.macros.description: The ingredient's `per` times the quantity. Derived; a reader recomputes it.

meal.id.short: The slot's identifier within a plan.
meal.id.description: The slot's identifier within a plan: `train.m1`, `train.f2`, `rest.m3`. The same slot ids run through every stack of a rotation (only the plates change), which is how a day's log stays whole when the stack changes. A meal on its own has no slot and reads `shelf.m1`.

meal.code.short: The short code, never shown to a person.
meal.code.description: A short code for telemetry and Coach: `M1`, `M2`, `PRE`, `POST`, `F1`. Never shown to a person; a screen that names a meal uses `meal.name`.

meal.name.description: What the meal is called, as it appears on Today and in History.

meal.kind.description: `meal` (the default) or `fuel`. Fuel has no portions and no stated macros, keeps its anchor, offset and alert, is logged, and never counts as a meal or adds to a total.

meal.anchor.short: What the meal's time hangs from.
meal.anchor.description: What the meal's time hangs from. `forward` chains off the meal before it (the first forward meal of the day sits on wake time); `before_session`, `at_session` and `after_session` are pinned to the session and do not move when the morning runs late. Rest days have no session, so every rest meal is `forward`. Every training day has one meal (not fuel) anchored `before_session`: the carb surge. Required inside a stack; absent on a meal on its own.

meal.offset_minutes.description: For `forward`, minutes after the previous forward meal (0 for the first). For `before_session` and `after_session`, minutes before or after the session. For `at_session`, 0. Never negative. Required inside a stack; absent on a meal on its own.

meal.prep_lead_minutes.short: How long before the meal the start-cooking alert fires.
meal.prep_lead_minutes.description: How many minutes before the meal's time the start-cooking alert fires; 0 for none.

meal.portions.short: What is on the plate (an array of `portion`).
meal.portions.description: What is on the plate, in order. One of `portions` or `stated` is required on a meal; fuel has neither.

meal.stated.short: Typed figures for a plate that was never weighed (a `macros`).
meal.stated.description: Grams of protein, carbs and fat typed in for a plate the person knows the numbers of but does not weigh. Read only when `portions` is empty.

meal.macros.short: What the plate comes to, derived (a `macros`).
meal.macros.description: The sum of the portions, or `stated` when there are none. Derived; never written by a plan file.

meal.note.description: One line under the name, on Today and on the shelf.
meal.note.example: Blue box. Microwave 2½ min, stir, 1½ min.

meal.steps.description: How it is made, one step per entry.

meal.source.description: The example plan, Coach, the person's own hands, or an import.

stack.id.short: The stack's identifier on the shelf.
stack.id.description: A UUID for a kept stack. A stack inside a plan file has none; its position and name identify it.

stack.name.description: What the stack is called ("The Base", "Rice Bowls", "Meet week"). The first stack of a plan has one too.

stack.note.description: One line under the name. An imported stack's note carries the plan's name and notes.
stack.note.example: Teriyaki chicken at lunch, crispy tofu after training.

stack.training.short: The training day's meals (an array of `meal`).
stack.training.description: The training day's meals, in the order eaten. Either day may be empty only if the other is not.

stack.rest.short: The rest day's meals (an array of `meal`).
stack.rest.description: The rest day's meals, in the order eaten, all anchored `forward`.

stack.source.description: The example rotation, Coach, the person's own hands, or an import.

stack.origin.short: The plan the stack came in with.
stack.origin.description: For an imported stack, the name of the plan file it came in with, so a four-stack import reads as one thing.

plan.name.description: What the plan is called. A single stack imports under its own name.

plan.notes.short: A sentence or two about the plan.
plan.notes.description: A sentence or two about the plan. A plan written by a model carries the caveat here ("General nutrition information for healthy adults, not medical advice…"), so it shows on the import preview and under each stack.
plan.notes.example: A four-week meal-prep loop. When Week 4 ends, start Week 1 again.

plan.stacks.short: The stacks, in rotation order (an array of `stack`).
plan.stacks.description: The stacks, in rotation order, one per calendar week. The first runs first; when the last ends the first runs again. In plan file format 1 the key `weeks` is the older spelling and reads as the same thing.

plan.meals.short: Meals on their own (an array of `meal` with no anchor).
plan.meals.description: Meals for the Meals shelf, with no place in a day. A file may carry only these.

plan.ingredients.short: Ingredients the app doesn't have built in (an array of `ingredient`).
plan.ingredients.description: Ingredients the app doesn't have built in, declared once and referenced by id from portions. A file may carry only these. In plan file format 1 the app reads the key `ingredients` from 0.9.1 and `foods` (the spelling 0.9 reads, and the one writers still write until 0.9.1 is the oldest build in use) as the same thing; a file with both is read by `ingredients`.

plan.week_anchor.short: The calendar week the first stack ran.
plan.week_anchor.description: The start of the calendar week that counts as the first stack's, from which the rotation is counted. Set by the app; "run Rice Bowls this week" moves it. Absent on a single-stack plan and in a plan file.

plan.meals_per_day.training.short: How many meals a training day holds.
plan.meals_per_day.training.description: How many meal slots (not fuel) a training day holds. Five by default, 2 to 8.

plan.meals_per_day.rest.short: How many meals a rest day holds.
plan.meals_per_day.rest.description: How many meal slots (not fuel) a rest day holds. Five by default, 2 to 8.

plan.target.description: The daily targets every stack is measured against. Offered on import, never applied silently.

plan.schedule.short: The clock the plan is built on (a `schedule`).
plan.schedule.description: The times and days the plan is built on. Offered on import, never applied silently.

schedule.wake.description: When the first meal of the day is, as `HH:MM` 24-hour local time.

schedule.session.short: When the first working set is, `HH:MM`.
schedule.session.description: When the training session starts (the first working set), `HH:MM`. Rest days have no session.

schedule.latest_meal.short: The latest a meal may land, `HH:MM`.
schedule.latest_meal.description: The latest a meal may land, `HH:MM`. The day compresses rather than cross it.

schedule.training_weekdays.short: Which weekdays are training days, 1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday.
schedule.training_weekdays.description: Which weekdays are training days, as 1 = Sunday through 7 = Saturday. Every other day is a rest day.

schedule.min_gap_minutes.short: The closest two meals may sit.
schedule.min_gap_minutes.description: The closest two meals may sit when the day compresses. 120 by default.

schedule.home_timezone.short: The home time zone, as an IANA name.
schedule.home_timezone.description: The time zone the times are in, as an IANA name. A day run away from home is a travel day.

target.training.description: Grams of protein, carbs and fat for a training day.

target.rest.description: Grams of protein, carbs and fat for a rest day.

target.formula.description: Where the numbers came from: typed by hand, Coach's formula, or a file.

day.key.short: The calendar day, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the day's zone.
day.key.description: The calendar day as `YYYY-MM-DD` in the day's own time zone. The document's identity.

day.timezone.short: The zone the day ran in, as an IANA name.
day.timezone.description: The time zone the day ran in. A day keeps its zone when the phone moves, so a day in progress is not abandoned at a border.

day.type.description: Whether the day ran as a training day or a rest day, after any override.

day.stack.short: The stack the day ran on, by name.
day.stack.description: The name of the stack of the rotation the day ran on, stamped at the first log and again if the person says otherwise that day. Absent on a single-stack plan.

day.travel.short: Whether the day was a travel day.
day.travel.description: Whether the day ran away from home, set by the zone or by hand.

day.meal_count.short: How many meals the day ran on, when not the plan's.
day.meal_count.description: How many meal slots the day ran on when the person set it for the day; absent when it was the plan's count.

day.session_start.description: When training actually began, set by logging the session's fuel or by hand; the block around training moves with it.

day.target.short: The target the day ran against (a `macros`).
day.target.description: The daily target as it stood when the day was logged.

day.consumed.description: The sum of every logged meal's `consumed`. Derived.

day.meals.short: Every meal of the day and what happened to it (an array of `day.meal`).
day.meals.description: Every slot the day had, logged or not, in the day's order.

day.meal.id.description: The slot the entry is filed under, matching `meal.id` in the plan.

day.meal.planned_at.short: When the app said the meal was due.
day.meal.planned_at.description: The time the app showed for the meal at the moment it was logged. History scores timing against this.

day.meal.eaten_at.description: When the meal was logged as eaten. Never in the future; absent when it was not eaten.

day.meal.skipped.description: Whether the person skipped the meal on purpose.

day.meal.snoozed_minutes.description: How many minutes the meal was pushed by "not yet" before it was eaten or the day ended.

day.meal.landed.short: The meal as it was when eaten, frozen (a `meal`).
day.meal.landed.description: The meal as it stood at the moment it was logged: name, portions or stated figures, anchor, code, kind. Written once, never rewritten.

day.meal.consumed.description: The macros of the landed meal.

day.meal.timezone.short: The zone the meal was logged in.
day.meal.timezone.description: The phone's time zone when the meal was logged, which can differ from the day's.

event.action.short: The app's name for what happened.
event.action.description: The app's name for what happened, lower case with underscores, the same string the app's telemetry has always sent.

event.category.description: The ECS category the action falls under; the app's actions are all `process` events from the person's point of view, or `configuration` for settings.
